stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is launching a monthly in-store injection service for a medication that Massachusetts does not authorize a pharmacist to administer. The written protocol has the pharmacist complete the sale and hand the prefilled syringe to the patient at the register, has the patient carry it to the consultation room and hand it back unopened, and then has the pharmacist give the injection. The protocol assigns the patient no preparation, storage, or handling role, sets no interval between the handover and the return, and runs the same way for every patient. A staff pharmacist asks whether the protocol is acceptable. Which assessment is best?

choices.text: The formal characterization of the handover as a completed dispensing controls, so no administration restriction is engaged.
The patient's possession of the syringe makes the patient rather than the pharmacist the administering party.
The protocol is impermissible, because arranging the steps this way indirectly circumvents the administration restriction.
A valid prescription and a lawful dispensing together authorize the pharmacist to administer the medication.
Responsibility for the arrangement rests with whoever designed the protocol, not with the pharmacist following it.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.01(2) forbids a licensee from processing a prescription, dispensing a drug or device, or administering a controlled substance or vaccine in a manner intended, either directly or indirectly, to circumvent any law or regulation governing the practice of pharmacy. M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 authorizes pharmacist administration only through the three routes in clause (c), and this service is outside them. Purpose is inferred from what the arrangement does rather than from anything the participants say: the handover gives the patient no preparation, storage, or handling task, allows no interval, and is scripted for every patient, so the only work that step performs is to interpose a nominal dispensing before an injection the pharmacist still gives. Splitting one planned pharmacist injection into labelled steps changes neither who administers nor what the restriction reaches.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. 247 CMR 9.01(2) reaches the manner of the arrangement, so the label attached to one step does not decide whether the administration restriction is engaged.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The pharmacist performs the injection. Momentary possession does not move the administering act to the patient.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The possession step performs no function other than interposing a dispensing, which is the indirect manner of circumvention the standard prohibits.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Lawful prescribing and lawful dispensing are separate authorities from pharmacist administration, which M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 grants only through its enumerated routes.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. 247 CMR 9.01(2) binds the licensee who carries out the arrangement, not only whoever designed it.

related_facts: 247 CMR 9.01(2) expressly reaches indirect circumvention, so an arrangement can violate it even where every step is separately describable.

M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1 clause (c) authorizes pharmacist administration only under department regulations for mental health and substance use disorder treatment at a prescriber's direction, under a prescription for testosterone for gender-affirming care, or under a prescription for treating or preventing sexually transmitted infections or preventing HIV.
Purpose under the standard is inferred from what a step actually accomplishes, not only from what participants say about it.
explanation.mpje_trap: Reconstruct the integrated transaction and ask what independent clinical or handling function each intermediate step performs. A step that performs none is evidence of the manner the rule prohibits.

reasoning_steps: Confirm the pharmacist, not the patient, performs the injection.
Confirm the planned service falls outside the pharmacist-administration routes in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 1.
Ask what independent clinical or handling function the momentary patient possession performs.
Apply the direct-or-indirect circumvention standard in 247 CMR 9.01(2) to the arrangement as a whole.
